statement: arc-15 had already landed a minimal 3-variant ScanMode (Files/Diff/All) in crates/enforcer-scan/src/modes.rs as a skeleton placeholder; f01's owns claim on that exact file meant superseding it in place, not adding a sibling module. A grep across crates/ for `modes::`/`ScanMode`/`request_for_mode` found zero external consumers, confirming the supersession was same-file and non-breaking.
why: The workpack's file-disjointness model assumes each owns path starts empty or append-only; when a skeleton crate (arc-15) pre-populates a file another workpack (f01) owns outright, the safe move is to verify zero external references before rewriting, not to assume the skeleton is load-bearing elsewhere.
howToApply: Before rewriting a file another lane's skeleton already populated, grep the whole workspace for every public symbol the existing file exports; zero hits outside the file itself means a full rewrite is safe, otherwise treat it as an additive extension instead.

statement: enforcer-scan's fan-out engine (engine::run) has no per-rule Tier tagging on its emitted Finding/Violation values (only Severity), and enforcer-rules' RuleRegistry (which does carry Tier) is only a dev-dependency of enforcer-scan, not a runtime one. modes.rs therefore cannot do real tier-based rule *selection* inside the engine without a Cargo.toml edit outside its owns; it instead defines TierFilter as a typed post-hoc filter over emitted rule ids, letting a caller (test, or a future MCP/CLI wiring) supply the rule_id-to-Tier classifier.
why: Strict owns discipline (modes.rs/tests/modes.rs/fixtures only, no Cargo.toml or engine.rs edits) meant real tier-filtered scanning had to be provable without touching the engine's dependency graph or its Finding shape.
howToApply: When a workpack's typed selector needs data (like rule tier) that the engine it drives doesn't expose yet, express the selector as a structural filter taking a classifier as input/parameter rather than reaching into a sibling crate's production dependencies; prove the real behavior in the owned test file using a dev-dependency (already present) to supply that classifier.

statement: ScanModeError in crates/enforcer-scan/src/modes.rs implements std::fmt::Display/std::error::Error by hand instead of deriving thiserror::Error, because enforcer-scan does not depend on the thiserror crate directly (only enforcer-core does) and adding it would require a Cargo.toml edit outside f01's owns (src/modes.rs, tests/modes.rs, tests/fixtures/modes/**).
why: The workpack requires 'a typed thiserror error' for boundary rejection; DecodeError (enforcer_core::error::DecodeError) IS thiserror-derived and modes.rs wraps/defers to it for scope validation, so the typed-error doctrine is honored via composition without a new direct dependency.
howToApply: When a workpack mandates a thiserror-style typed error but the owned crate lacks the thiserror dependency and Cargo.toml is out of scope, hand-implement Display+std::error::Error (matching thiserror's #[error(...)] message shape) and wrap the workspace's existing thiserror-derived error type (enforcer_core::error::DecodeError) via a From impl rather than editing Cargo.toml.

statement: cargo test -p enforcer-scan --test modes exits 0 with 9 passing tests proving: scoped/quick modes do not report a T1-RUSTERR.1 violation planted outside their scoped subdir; scoped/full modes both report the same violation when planted inside scope; full always reports regardless of location; an unknown mode string is rejected both via serde deserialization and FromStr, never silently defaulted; the no-arg ScanRequest::default() resolves to Scoped with a Paths (never All) scope_request.
why: This is the literal proof row scan-modes-select from docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md row f01, gating DONE for this workpack.
howToApply: Future workers touching crates/enforcer-scan/src/modes.rs must keep cargo test -p enforcer-scan --test modes green; the fixtures at tests/fixtures/modes/violation_outside_scope and tests/fixtures/modes/violation_inside_scope are the load-bearing fail/pass pair for the scope-honoring assertion and must not be deleted or have their planted .unwrap() removed.
